simple.meaning: צָפָה (tsâphâh) appears 37 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced in connection with kingship.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Genesis, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 2 Kings, Job, and 11 more, beginning at Genesis 31:49. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, kingship, city.

definitions.short: properly, to lean forward, i.e. to peer into the distance; by implication, to observe , await
definitions.usage: behold, espy, look up (well), wait for, (keep the) watch(-man).
definitions.full: H6822. tsaphah I. [ צָפָה ] 37 verb look out or about, spy keep watch (Late Hebrew id. , Pi`el hope ;; Ethiopic III. hope ); — Qal 28 Imperfect 3masculine singular jussive וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ בֵּינִי יִצֶף Gen 31:49 (J) may ׳י keep watch between me and thee (that the covenant be kept = ׳א וגו ׳עֵד 31:50 ); 3feminine plural תִּצְמֶּי֑נָה בַּגּוֺיִם עֵינָיו Psa 66:9 his eyes keep watch upon the nations; Participle active לַצַּדִּיק רָשָׁע֫ צוֺפֶה 37:32 a wicked man spieth upon the righteous ; Cant 7:5 the town which looketh toward ( מְּנֵי ) Damascus; feminine צוֺפִיָּה Prov 31:27 she keepeth watch of (with accusative); plural וְטוֺבִים רָעִים צֹפוֺת י ׳עֵינֵי 15:3 ; elsewhere as substantive watchman , absolute צֹפֶה 2Sam 13:34 +; plural צֹפִים 1Sam 14:16 +, suffix צֹפָיו Isa 56:10 Qr (Kt צפו ), צֹפַיִךְ 52:8 ; — 1Sam 14:16 ; 2Sam 13:34 8 t. Samuel Kings, Ezek 33:2 , 6 (twice in verse); Isa 52:8 , so in צֹפִים שְׂדֵה Num 23:14 (JE); figurative of prophets Hosea 9:8 ; Jer 6:17 ; Ezek 3:17 ; 33:7 ; Isa 56:10 ; — צוֺפִים 1Sam 1:1 see צוּפִי ; Passive participle צָפוּ (Manuscripts and Qr צָפוּי ), Job 15:22 spied out (and brought) to ( אֱלֵי ) the sword (Em Bi Perles Anal. 29 צָפוּן compare Di Bu). Pi`el Perfect 1plural צִמִּינוּ Lam 4:17 ; Imperfect 1singular אֲצַמֶּה Micah 7:7 +; Imperative masculine singular צַמֵּה Nahum 2:2 , feminine singular צַמִּי Jer 48:19 ; Participle מְצַמֶּה 1Sam 4:13 ; Isa 21:6 ; plural suffix מְצַמֶּיךָ Micah 7:4 ; — watch ( closely ), וְצ ׳עִמְדִי אֶלרֶּֿרֶךְ Jer 48:19 , דֶֿרֶךְ׳צ Nahum 2:2 ; + אֶל of person expected Lam 4:17 ; figurative ׳בְּי אֲצַמֶּה Micah 7:7 ; absolute literal 1Sam 4:13 ; figurative Hab 2:1 I will look forth , to see ( לִרְאוֺת ) what he will say; Psa 5:4 I will look out (expectantly); participle as noun = watchman Isa 21:6 ; Micah 7:4 .

occurrences.englishText: and Mizpah, for he said, “Yahweh watch between me and you, when we are absent one from another.
When he came, behold, Eli was sitting on his seat by the road watching, for his heart trembled for God’s ark. When the man came into the city and told about it, all the city cried out.
The watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and behold, the multitude melted away and scattered.
But Absalom fled. The young man who kept the watch lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold, many people were coming by way of the hillside behind him.
Now David was sitting between the two gates; and the watchman went up to the roof of the gate to the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, a man running alone.
The watchman cried, and told the king. The king said, “If he is alone, there is news in his mouth.” He came closer and closer.
The watchman saw another man running; and the watchman called to the gatekeeper, and said, “Behold, a man running alone!”
The watchman saw another man running; and the watchman called to the gatekeeper, and said, “Behold, a man running alone!”
The watchman said, “I think the running of the first one is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.”
Now the watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel, and he spied the company of Jehu as he came, and said, “I see a company.”
So one went on horseback to meet him, and said, “the king says, ‘Is it peace?’ ”
The watchman said, “He came to them, and isn’t coming back. The driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi, for he drives furiously.”
He doesn’t believe that he will return out of darkness.

He rules by his might forever.

She looks well to the ways of her household,
For the Lord said to me, “Go, set a watchman. Let him declare what he sees.

I set watchmen over you, saying, ‘Listen to the sound of the trumpet!’ But they said, ‘We will not listen!’
Inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way and watch.

“Son of man, I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel. Therefore hear the word from my mouth, and warn them from me.
“Son of man, speak to the children of your people, and tell them, ‘When I bring the sword on a land, and the people of the land take a man from among them, and set him for their watchman;

But if the watchman sees the sword come, and doesn’t blow the trumpet, and the people aren’t warned, and the sword comes, and takes any person from among them; he is taken away in his iniquity, but his blood I will require at the watchman’s hand.’

But if the watchman sees the sword come, and doesn’t blow the trumpet, and the people aren’t warned, and the sword comes, and takes any person from among them; he is taken away in his iniquity, but his blood I will require at the watchman’s hand.’
“So you, son of man: I have set you a watchman to the house of Israel. Therefore hear the word from my mouth, and give them warnings from me.
A prophet watches over Ephraim with my God.
The best of them is like a brier.
But as for me, I will look to Yahweh.
For Yahweh restores the excellency of Jacob, as the excellency of Israel; for the destroyers have destroyed them, and ruined their vine branches.
I will stand at my watch, and set myself on the ramparts, and will look out to see what he will say to me, and what I will answer concerning my complaint.
